bug_semantics: POST /api/provider-nodes/validate accepts caller-controlled baseUrl and apiKey, makes server-side requests to baseUrl-derived provider endpoints, and forwards the supplied secret in Authorization headers. The later assertPublicUrl mitigation checks only the URL hostname string: it neither resolves DNS nor revalidates redirect destinations, and its IPv4-mapped IPv6 regex expects a dotted quad even though WHATWG URL canonicalization has already converted that quad to hextets. A mapped loopback or link-local literal, a domain resolving to a private address, or a redirect can therefore reach internal services. The custom-embedding path reflects the first 200 bytes of a non-2xx response other than 401/403; the other paths expose status, timing, and error differences for blind port scanning.
flaw_origin: Commit 0a28f9f924d2dc53027a910679ee3cff3e63a59c created the validation route and, in the same minimal change, read baseUrl/apiKey from the request, interpolated baseUrl into /models, fetched it without any destination policy, and forwarded apiKey as a Bearer token. That is the first complete attacker-controlled outbound-request mechanism. Commit 0b8bed5793c7a7c9beb7a5db7368720907f61ebc later added the custom-embedding branch and 200-byte error-body disclosure; 090886ced9a3481837f5687ec66da7d9f33eea08 later connected a hostname-only guard; and 8ac631d6158c0f04976a0d0f7ca9ec2b981efeb5 later added an ineffective mapped-IPv6 check. Those later changes altered impact or attempted mitigation but did not originate the SSRF sink, which was already exploitable in their parents.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names author and committer decolua <decoluadt@example.com> and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: Advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cqgh-7h49-q3mr; first-party report: https://github.com/decolua/9router/issues/3293; proposed remediation: https://github.com/decolua/9router/pull/3313. `git log master -S 'const modelsUrl = `${baseUrl.replace' -- .../validate/route.js` identifies only 0a28f9f924d2dc53027a910679ee3cff3e63a59c for the original sink; its patch creates src/app/api/provider-nodes/validate/route.js and adds request parsing, `${baseUrl...}/models`, fetch(), and `Authorization: Bearer ${apiKey}` together. `git ls-tree -r --name-only 1b14c9d66bd5bfa6f2a2980ab0469258bf2e2eda -- src/app/api/provider-nodes/validate/route.js` returns no path, directly proving the route and vulnerable mechanism are absent from the immediate parent tree. `git cat-file commit 0a28f9...` proves the full parent, human author/committer, and trailer-free BIC message. `git describe --contains 0a28f9...` returns `v0.2.52~2`; `git tag --contains 0a28f9... --sort=version:refname` starts at v0.2.52 (v0.2.43 is absent) and continues through v0.5.55, establishing the introduction boundary. At current master 699edac3273e13d4744bc46f6082618f08560702, src/app/api/provider-nodes/validate/route.js:57-58 takes baseUrl/apiKey, :69-76 calls the guard, :84-90 performs the custom-embedding request with the Bearer token, and :100-104 reflects 200 bytes; src/shared/utils/ssrfGuard.js:39-55 performs only textual checks and contains the unreachable dotted-quad mapped-address branch. A direct Node smoke invocation prints `[::ffff:7f00:1]` followed by `ALLOWED` for `http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/`. GitHub's current master API also resolves to 699edac3273e13d4744bc46f6082618f08560702. PR #3313 remains open with merged_at=null; its sole head commit d5277737de24aba6a297d0c0d4fdda41cd71f535 is based on 699edac... and replaces remote route fetches with a DNS-aware, per-connect/redirect-validating dispatcher. Thus d5277737... is recorded only as the direct proposed fix, while no upstream fix_sha or patched tag exists.
reasoning: The vulnerability lifecycle begins with 0a28f9..., because that smallest commit first makes a caller-controlled URL an authenticated server-side fetch destination and forwards the caller's apiKey. Its immediate parent has no validation-route file at all. The later embedding commit increases confidentiality impact, and later guard commits try to constrain the already-existing sink but leave mapped IPv6, DNS resolution, and redirects open; an incomplete later mitigation cannot replace the earlier causal BIC when its own parent is already exploitable. Release reachability agrees: the BIC first appears in v0.2.52 and remains an ancestor of the latest v0.5.55 tag, while there is no patched release boundary. The proposed PR head is not merged, so fix_sha is null and direct_fix_sha identifies only the reviewable patch commit. Applying the BIC-only attribution rule, the raw 0a28f9... commit object has a human author/committer and no AI marker, yielding NOT_AI regardless of signals on later mitigation or proposed-fix commits. Upstream remains unpatched.
remaining_gap: Upstream is still unpatched: PR #3313 is open and unmerged, current master remains 699edac3273e13d4744bc46f6082618f08560702, and no patched tag or upstream fix commit exists. d5277737de24aba6a297d0c0d4fdda41cd71f535 is only the direct proposed fix head.
